bull.b: The long-dated Rockdale lease shifts part of Riot’s growth profile toward contracted infrastructure revenue rather than relying solely on Bitcoin mining. Its scale, duration, and targeted high NOI margin could improve earnings visibility and support durable cash generation as capacity is delivered.

The combined lease portfolio creates a meaningful recurring revenue base tied to data center capacity and customer contracts. Scaling from mining into leased infrastructure can diversify Riot’s business model, strengthen customer relationships, and provide a platform for further site expansion.

Low reported power and direct production costs are an important competitive advantage in Bitcoin mining, where electricity and operating efficiency directly affect margins. Maintaining this cost position can help Riot remain viable through network competition and changing Bitcoin economics.

bear.b: The current cost structure is not translating strong revenue growth into sustainable profits. Deep losses across operating earnings reduce internal funding capacity, increase dependence on financing or asset monetization, and make future results highly sensitive to operating conditions and execution.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that Riot is consuming cash while pursuing expansion rather than funding investment from recurring operations. Continued cash burn can constrain flexibility, increase funding needs, and heighten the consequences of delays or weaker project economics.

The planned data center buildout requires substantial capital before the projected contracted revenues are realized. Riot’s stated use of Bitcoin sales and project financing increases reliance on external funding and asset monetization, making execution and capital access central to the growth plan.
